meta.note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Barkpark Unified Aesthetic. HAND-EDIT THIS FILE ONLY. Every surface token (Studio CSS vars, web @theme, Go semrole/taskboard artifact, paper-surface.css, pdrender) is GENERATED from here by W1.2 emitters — never edit generated output; regenerate it. Language-neutral: colors are HSL channels (H S% L%) so per-surface emitters can convert and the '/ alpha' soft-tint machinery + WCAG gate survive.
meta.colorFormat: HSL channels 'H S% L%' (no hsl() wrapper) so emitters can splice into hsl(<channels> / <alpha>) for soft tints
meta.outOfScope: emitters, drift gate, surface adoption (W1.2 / W2+)

_convention.form: Each role has { light, dark } as HSL channels. softAlpha derives status soft-tint fills: hsl(<role channels> / <softAlpha[theme]>).

strongAlpha._note: warn carries a -strong variant in the cloud source; emitters derive it from this alpha over the warn channels.

primary-hover._role: evergreen brand, hover tone — darker in light, lighter in dark (standard hover shift)

accent._role: warm amber, decorative — NOT a status

reading-accent._role: warm reading accent — the paper terracotta, tokenized

code._role: code-block fg/bg — mint syntax tones for the paper code frame (pdrender GenCodeFg/GenCodeBg). Hex directly (adaptive light/dark); read by pdrenderGo alongside the reading family.

paper._note: Paper reading-surface `--paper-*` theme palette, captured VERBATIM from api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css (rgba stays rgba, hex stays hex — like color.code; NO HSL conversion, NO cross-family dedup this wave — that is ts-w3 compiler business). TWO variants because the surface is theme-swapped two different ways with DELIBERATELY divergent hairlines: 'surface' = the shared paper-surface.css tokens the EDIT surfaces (Studio + the embedder bundle) stamp via html[data-theme] (emitted by paperBlock into the GENERATED marker region on the html[data-theme=light|dark] + bare-fallback selectors); 'reader' = the bulldocs.html.heex /papers reader-skin overrides (emitted by bulldocsBlock), which theme-swap via prefers-color-scheme and DIVERGE on --paper-rule (solid #dde7e2 light / rgba(231,237,233,0.13) dark) vs surface's rgba(21,33,29,0.09) / rgba(231,237,233,0.10) so the reader hairline reads cleaner on the article ground. reader.light stamps 7 roles; reader.dark re-skins 10 (it also owns ink-faint/chrome-bg/chrome-border the reader inherits from the shared light fallback). --paper-font-* and the callout --bp-tone-* are NOT here — fonts stay hand-authored in paper-surface.css, callouts are ts-w2's paperCallout family.

mailChrome._note: Mail-client popup chrome for the /papers Email view (bulldocs.html.heex #bp-mailapp — the ONLY copy). 6 roles × light/dark, captured VERBATIM (hex stays hex). These skin the mail WINDOW (title bar / toolbar / sender header / body frame) — theme-aware like a real dark mail client showing a light HTML email; the served email BYTES never change with the theme. Emitted by bulldocsBlock into the same reader-skin marker region (the --mail-* var-definition block is relocated there; grep-proven the sole definition). NO HSL, NO dedup this wave.

cliCalloutNeutral._role: neutral callout tone for the pdrender WASM reader (Theme.Callout 'neutral' bar/body) — the neutral peer of color.status's ok/info/warn/danger. Hex directly (adaptive light/dark); read by pdrenderGo ONLY (emitted as GenToneNeutral). Verbatim capture of pdrender's hand toneNeut; the w3 compiler reconciles it with the status family.

status._note: The four semantic roles ok/info/warn/danger. 'ok' green is health/live-dot and is DELIBERATELY distinct from lifecycle 'done' teal (see lifecycle section). Emitters expose --ok/--info/--warn/--danger and derive -soft (softAlpha) fills; warn also gets -strong (strongAlpha).

onStatus._note: On-fill foregrounds for the four status roles — the white text that sits ON a filled --ok/--warn/--danger/--info chip. Studio-only (emitted by studioBlock ONLY; no other surface consumes them). danger-fg is asymmetric (98% light / 100% dark, mirroring the live shadcn --destructive-fg); the rest are pure white both themes.

studioChrome._note: Studio-only zinc/chrome ladder aliases (shadcn zinc shades that have no exact base-role token). Values are HSL channels 'H S% L%' OR a 'var(--role)' reference where an emitted base role already carries the exact value (border-muted light = --border; fg-accent dark = --text). Emitted by studioBlock ONLY. Consumed via var(--bg-accent|--border-muted|--fg-dim|--fg-accent|--surface-raised|--border-subtle) across Studio chrome. fg-dim is AA-tuned: contrast(--fg-dim,--bg) >= 4.5 both modes while staying the dimmest text tier. surface-raised = elevated card fill (visibly above --bg in dark); border-subtle = hairline between --border-muted and --bg.

cliChrome._note: CLI/TUI chrome roles emitted ONLY into the sibling internal/semrole/chrome_gen.go (via cliChromeGo) — the status/lifecycle tokens_gen.go stays byte-stable. Nine NEW AdaptiveColor roles carry {light,dark} HEX directly. Five REUSE roles are 'var(--role)' references the emitter RESOLVES to the target role's hex (chrome-primary-cta → evergreen --primary, NOT the legacy #2563eb blue; chrome-on-primary → adaptive --primary-fg). Call sites are threaded in a later wave; the lit-allows stay for now. RETINT (theme-system D19, supersedes ts-w2b's byte-exact blue capture): the accent/selection blue family is now PRIMARY-DERIVED evergreen so a theme change moves CLI/TUI chrome with every other surface — chrome-accent = hslToHex(color.primary) per mode (light #1e5243, dark #75c7ac from 160 42% 62%); chrome-selection-fg light = same #1e5243, dark = hslToHex(color.primary-hover.dark 160 42% 70%) = #92d3bd; chrome-selection-bg = color.primary mixed 10% over the mode bg, flattened to a solid gamma-sRGB hex (light: primary.light 10% over #ffffff = #e9eeec; dark: primary.dark 10% over hslToHex(color.bg.dark 240 10% 3.9%)=#09090b = #141c1b). chrome-cursor-bg stays zinc (a keystroke cursor, not brand); color.primary itself is untouched.

presence._note: Categorical presence-avatar palette (8 fixed hues, hex, theme-invariant). NOT a status role — a phash2 of the user id indexes into this list, so the hue IS categorical identity, not semantics. Emitted as an Elixir VALUE list (BarkparkWeb.Studio.TokensGen.presence_palette/0), NOT a CSS var — the concrete hex is picked/compared at runtime. Mirrors presence_state.ex @colors 1:1.

sheetCf._note: Categorical Sheets swatch palettes (hex, theme-invariant). PERSISTED DATA: a chosen swatch is stored on the cell/rule/tab (phx-value-bg / set_tab_color) and compared for selection state — the concrete hex MUST survive, so these emit as Elixir VALUE lists (BarkparkWeb.Studio.TokensGen.sheet_cf_backgrounds/0 + sheet_tab_colors/0), never CSS vars. 'background' = the pastel cell/rule fills; 'tab' = the saturated per-tab dots (read best more vivid). Mirror sheet_grid.ex 1:1.

matchQuality._note: Categorical match-quality data-viz SPECTRUM (7 ordered stops, fuzzy→exact, theme-invariant). The web finder's search-match legend gradient — a decorative spectrum, NOT a status role: binding it onto ok/warn/danger/info would destroy the ordered fuzzy→exact distinctness (mirrors the presence / Sheets-CF categorical precedent). Stored as HSL channels (not hex like presence) because it feeds a CSS linear-gradient and is never compared for equality — the HSL triples are byte-faithful to the original finder.tsx literal. Emitted as a VALUE list into web/lib/tokens.gen.ts (matchQuality), consumed by web/components/finder.tsx's HighlightLegend gradient. Mirrors the old inline 7-stop hsl() rainbow 1:1.

pdrenderChart._note: Categorical pdrender chart-series palette (6 fixed hues, hex, theme-invariant). NOT a status role — the per-series colour cycle the terminal bar/line chart legend paints under a TrueColor profile (blue/pink/green/amber/violet/cyan, a legible categorical set), cycled by index like presence. Emitted as a Go VALUE slice (GenChartSeries in internal/pdrender/tokens_gen.go), consumed by internal/pdrender/chart.go's chartSeriesColor; byte-faithful to the former hand literal so the render is unchanged. Mirrors the presence / matchQuality categorical precedent (a passthrough family — D21).

pdrenderHeatmap._note: Categorical pdrender heatmap palette (hex, theme-invariant). NOT a status role — a GitHub-contribution-style dark→bright green heat scale. TWO consumers, both in internal/pdrender/heatmap.go: (1) base→peak ENDPOINTS drive heatTrueColor's per-cell linear interpolation under a TrueColor profile (legacy 2-endpoint ramp, byte-faithful to the #0d1117/#39d353 literals so that render is unchanged); (2) ramp = 4 discrete shade steps (light→full) matched 1:1 to the dual-encode glyph ladder for the quantile-binned calendar/matrix modes — ramp[3] == peak keeps the discrete scale visually consistent with the gradient peak. Emitted as Go consts + GenHeatRamp []lipgloss.Color in internal/pdrender/tokens_gen.go. A passthrough family (D21) — never derived per theme.

provider._note: Cloud-provider IDENTITY marks (charter azure-hetzner Decision 7): hetzner = a red-tinged tint, azure = a blue-tinged tint, each {light,dark} HEX so the mark clears contrast in both themes. IDENTITY ONLY — a provider tint may color a chip mark or a chip/row border, but NEVER a pill background: the semantic status roles (ok/warn/danger/info) stay the ONLY state voice, so provider identity never doubles as status (see cloud/DESIGN.md §5). Emitted as --provider-<kind> CSS custom properties into the app.css generated block AND as GenProviderMark AdaptiveColors in the Go CLI chrome sibling (internal/semrole/chrome_gen.go). A third provider is a new row here, not a design project.

authButton._note: Login/auth-page (session_html.ex) button fills — DECOUPLED from --primary so the fill stays a deeper green carrying light text (mirrors the Cloud dashboard). Emitted ONLY into session_html.ex's page-scoped .bp-auth block. bg/fg light are var(--primary)/var(--primary-fg) passthroughs; bgHover carries the auth-specific hover tone; dark bg is the standalone deep-green fill with white text.

statusChrome._note: Public status page (status_controller.ex) self-contained :root chrome palette. Standalone page rendered WITHOUT the Studio layout — the emitted :root tokens never cascade in — so it carries its own bg/fg/muted/card/line, theme-aware via prefers-color-scheme. Bespoke zinc shades (no exact base-role token); emitted ONLY into status_controller.ex's page-scoped block as HEX (byte-preserving the exact chrome).

statusHealth._note: Public status page health-severity DATA tones (status_controller.ex @labels + component dots). These convey OUTAGE SEVERITY as inline style hex — categorical DATA, not a CSS role. partial_outage (#ea580c) is an OUT-OF-MODEL minted tone sitting between warn-amber (degraded #d97706) and danger-red (major_outage #dc2626) — deliberately NOT recolored onto --warn/--danger so the severity distinction survives. 'unknown' is the neutral gray fallback for an unrecognised status. Emitted as an Elixir VALUE map (BarkparkWeb.Studio.TokensGen.status_health/0 + status_health_unknown/0).

errorPage._note: Error page (error_html.ex 404/500/…) FIXED-DARK palette. INTENTIONALLY always dark (a stark error card), NO theme switch — de-literalized WITHOUT becoming theme-aware (a theme-aware repoint would flip it light and break the intent). Emitted ONLY into error_html.ex's page-scoped :root block as single (non-theme) HEX values, byte-preserving.

graphCanvas._note: Obsidian-style documentation-graph canvas (web/components/graph-landing.tsx). INTENTIONALLY always dark — the graph reads as an Obsidian surface in BOTH light and dark modes (errorPage precedent), so a single hex, NO theme switch, no light variant. Emitted as the theme-invariant --color-graph-canvas @theme registration in web/app/globals.css (Tailwind v4 auto-generates the bg-graph-canvas utility from it).

readerInfo._note: The /sheets/:slug reader (sheets.html.heex) info-blue link + focus ring. Self-contained parchment reader (root tokens don't cascade), so it carries its own --info: a WCAG-safe darker blue-600 (#2563eb, clears 4.5:1 on the near-white parchment) in light, lifting to the info-role blue-500 (#3b82f6 = status.info) on the dark parchment. Semantic info-blue (NOT categorical). Emitted ONLY into sheets.html.heex's page-scoped :root/@media-dark block as HEX.

paperEmail._note: Paper EMAIL surface skin (theme-system Wave 1 CAPTURE — Decision D2/D3). Today's hand-typed evergreen email values, captured VERBATIM as hex (no HSL round-trip, no derivation). These deliberately DIVERGE from color.primary's HSL-derived Render.TokensGen brand (#1e5243 vs #1e5347) and color.border's #e4e4e7 vs the green-tinted #dde7e2 — email bytes ship to mail clients and consuming the drifted slots would retint the byte-locked golden. w3 reconciles the duplication; Wave 1's acceptance is emitted-bytes == today's-bytes. Consumed by render/palettes.ex (@brand/@brand_text/@rule/@page_bg + email_palette + article_palette var() fallbacks) and render/data_viz.ex (@email_*). Values are single light-only hex — the email surface has no dark mode.

paperCallout._note: Paper CALLOUT tone tints (theme-system Wave 1 CAPTURE — Decision D2). Two theme variants: 'light' = the five light {bg,fg} pairs from render/util.ex tone_palette/1 (mirrored by the --bp-tone-* light block in paper-surface.css); 'dark' = the five dark {bg,fg} pairs the bulldocs reader skin re-stamps (bulldocsBlock's prefers-color-scheme --bp-tone-* block, byte-mirroring paper-surface.css's html[data-theme=dark] .bp-paper-surface tones). Captured VERBATIM as hex. Semantic hues (success green / warning amber / danger red / info blue / neutral gray) pulled toward the evergreen ground so a toned callout sits IN the page. These are a DIFFERENT value set from color.status / Render.TokensGen.tone_* status roles — never substitute those. The light pairs emit as Render.TokensGen.callout/1; the dark pairs emit as the bulldocs reader-skin --bp-tone-* re-stamps.

reading.stack: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Charter, Georgia, "Source Serif 4", serif
reading._role: serif prose on the paper surface. Self-hosted (Source Serif 4 variable woff2, S9) on BOTH Studio (root.html.heex) and the /papers reader (bulldocs.html.heex), but named LAST-but-serif in the stack: Iowan Old Style still wins on macOS. The stack ORDER (Source Serif 4 → first) is a future one-line human-gated cutover (au-w5-reading-typography) — metadata only; emit reads only `.stack`.

chrome._note: UI chrome scale (Inter). Studio / web / TUI status text.

reading._note: Prose scale on the paper surface (serif). headingWeight applies to h1-h3.

elevation._note: Shadow ladder. Values are the LIGHT-theme shadows; dark is retuned per surface by emitters (deeper, lower-alpha). Recorded as CSS box-shadow strings.

lifecycle._note: Task-lifecycle vocabulary. RECONCILED 1:1 with internal/semrole/semrole.go (taskLifecycleRoles) + internal/taskboard (theme.go colors, components.go StatusGlyph, spinner.go asciiGlyph/frames, board.go life* consts). role '' = neutral/uncoloured (never a guess). 'color' here is the taskboard glyph hue (adaptive light/dark) and is INDEPENDENT of the semantic status palette above — notably 'done'/'closed' use TEAL, distinct from status.ok GREEN. Emitters that need the semantic role tone read color.status via 'role'.

_default._note: unknown lifecycle degrades to the neutral dot

in_progress._escalation: board-only: warms info -> warn -> danger as the 5-min claim lease burns

done._color_note: TEAL — deliberately distinct from status.ok green (#10b981/#34d399). Finished work recedes.

instanceLifecycle._note: Cloud INSTANCE lifecycle vocabulary (charter azure-hetzner Decision 7). Seven states an operator sees on a Barkpark instance, dual-emitted to the SPA (.bp-inst--<state> glyph-tone classes) and the Go CLI/TUI chrome (GenInstanceLifecycle in internal/semrole/chrome_gen.go). Entry shape mirrors a task-lifecycle entry (role + glyph + codepoint + asciiGlyph) with ONE deliberate difference: there is NO bespoke color. Each state's colour is READ THROUGH its semantic status role, so identity never doubles as status (Decision 7) and the status palette stays the single state voice. role maps: live→ok, degraded→warn, decommissioned→danger, provisioning/adopted→info, stopped/archived→'' (neutral → the muted-text tone). A later wave rewires app.js statusPill/bucketOf + the CLI table renderers onto these consts; THIS slice only DEFINES + EMITS.

_default._note: unknown instance state degrades to the neutral dot
